children: Brent crude futures have continued to strengthen this morning after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian warned yesterday that Tehran would never surrender to what he called Washington's bullying, sending oil prices higher.

The front-month contract expiring on September 30 for delivery in November climbed about 1.3% to reach $104 today, while the most-active Brent futures contract, which expires on October 30 with a December delivery, trades a little under $100 a barrel.

Pezeshkian said at the United Nations General Assembly yesterday that his country wouldn't allow freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while a U.S. blockade and sanctions are still in place. Hours before his speech, a cargo ship was attacked in the strait, killing an Indian sailor.

Pezeshkian's tone underscores "the difficulty in reaching a peace deal with Washington despite efforts to revive talks this week," said Helge Andre Martinsen, an energy analyst at Norwegian investment bank DNB Carnegie.

Investors are increasingly betting that the two sides are far apart and the impact of the conflict will last for months. The Brent futures contract expiring next August closed at $80.96 a barrel yesterday, the highest level since May. It's edging up further today.
